title: Compact cabinet-canonical pose and twist in a support-centered rotation chart
coverage_gap: A1 achieved 20/20 C and 20/20 E successes in the supplied development feedback, so there is no observed A1 failure cell to repair. Those finite samples do not establish perfect generalization. A2 failed all five E-LL episodes and A3 failed five E-HH plus four E-LH episodes, despite all candidates succeeding on C. The feedback provides native truncation categories, not contact trajectories; it cannot identify the mechanical cause. The remaining testable gap is whether A1's larger lifted representation is necessary, or whether a compact information-preserving pose chart can retain robustness at lower complete-system inference cost under the same training budget.
reusable_regularity: Preserve A1's static cabinet frame and orthogonal action mapping, but replace redundant geometric lifts by a 25-dimensional kinematic coordinate chart: cabinet-frame hand-minus-handle (3), handle-minus-goal (3), hand and handle finite differences (6), current/previous aperture (2), support-centered full SO(3) orientation log (3), full relative angular-motion log (3), world hand anchor (3), and cabinet sin/cos yaw (2). The orientation reference is the sign-aligned mean initial cabinet-local handle quaternion of the exact D_N. Centering the rotation chart at the closed handle avoids encoding a large constant handle-frame rotation and is not a planar-only approximation. No learned encoder, stage gates, articulated-frame fit or joint future channels are added. The common DP alone is learned from scratch.
dependencies_preserved: Let r=R^T(hand-handle), d=R^T(handle-goal). With the explicit world hand and observed cabinet rotation R, handle=hand-R*r and goal=hand-R*(r+d). Thus removing A1's explicit world goal does not remove its dependency; full robot, handle and goal world positions remain recoverable. The two translational differences similarly recover previous hand and handle.

Orientation is three-dimensional, not reduced to a single yaw. From the restored reference q0 and the SO(3) exponential of the current log one recovers the current cabinet-local orientation q0*exp(log). Given delta=log(inv(q_previous)*q_current), previous orientation is q_current*inv(exp(delta)). Multiplication by observed cabinet yaw recovers both world orientations up to the physically irrelevant quaternion sign.

The rotation chart is unique away from the standard pi cut. The task's closed-to-open motion motivates this chart, but failure at its cut is explicitly acknowledged. Quaternion normalization and hemisphere handling make ordinary q/-q changes equivalent.

Current/previous aperture, hand/handle motion, world hand, cabinet yaw, goal relation and complete handle orientation still expose fixed-finger alignment, world workspace, door sweep and contact dependencies. No fixed-end-effector rotation is changed by the action frame.

Only deterministic redundancies and declared absent object2 zeros are removed. Both whole causal observations are transformed independently. No future observations, masks, elapsed episode time, simulator geometry or planner are introduced.

All support fitting is restricted to the exact ten episodes of door__N10__rep0.
Observed cabinet sin/cos yaw, xyzw handle orientation, handle geom center, current/previous native state, world action cube and fixed gripper orientation.
Five LL/five HH support episodes and diagonal position-yaw coverage motivate preserving A1's canonical relations.

A consistent closed handle frame, separate hand/handle motion, and changing quaternion through the door swing support a reference-centered full orientation plus relative angular motion representation.
Another initial cabinet yaw and world pose; the orientation reference must be fitted after removing cabinet yaw, not from raw world quaternions.
Closed configuration used conceptually as a rotation-chart reference, not as a deployment image input.
Visible door articulation and nearby hand require retaining both object pose and hand-relative coordinates.
Large final door swing; orientation information is not discarded in favor of positions only.
Finite representation changes are allowed while preserving the common DP, optimizer, budget, native control semantics and action mask/loss.

expected_failure_signature: If explicit Euclidean distance lifts were crucial to A1's learned contact transitions, A4 may hover or descend incorrectly despite retaining enough information to reconstruct those distances. This would falsify the sufficiency of the compact inductive bias, not its mathematical recoverability.

The goal now enters through relative geometry instead of an absolute-goal bypass. Asymmetric C or E failures would indicate that the new factorization makes needed world-contact dependencies harder to learn under the fixed budget.

Near a relative rotation of pi, the minimal logarithmic chart has a cut; abrupt response or orientation-history inconsistency there is a specific representation failure mode. Full rotation columns in A1 do not have that chart cut.

Reducing the conditioner by twelve scalars reduces parameters, but rotation-log computations and denoiser-dominated execution may eliminate a latency advantage. Equal success with unchanged or higher fixed-method latency would not meet the intended cost benefit.
No A4 outcome or inference speed is claimed before formal evaluation. A1 remains immutable and eligible even if this single revision is negative.

required_runtime_fields.source: causal_context.raw_history [B,2,41] and raw_current [B,41], plus restored D_N initial-orientation reference
required_runtime_fields.action_frame: Unchanged from A1: xyz_encoded=Rz(cabinet_yaw_at_chunk_start)^T xyz_native, decoded with Rz. Same frame for all sixteen predictions, native dimensionless xyz still scales by 0.01 m, fourth scalar stays gripper. No action offsets, clipping or generated-future correction; the public executor alone clips in world coordinates and executes four steps.

support_fit.source: Only obs[0,7:11] and obs[0,39:41] from each exact D_N episode
support_fit.algorithm: Normalize each xyzw quaternion, left-multiply by inverse observed cabinet yaw, align sign with the first support reference, average the ten initial quaternions and renormalize. Store that orientation and count as JSON; register its conjugate and fixed metric scales as nonlearned buffers in build_modules. No actions, future trajectories or development states are used for fitting.
support_fit.inference: The reference is constant after restoration. Neither fit_support nor any temporal adaptation runs in deployment.

change_summary: One new revision slot derived from A1, trained from scratch without inherited weights. Keep static cabinet action frame, four local position/motion vectors and aperture. Replace two rotation columns plus their differences (12 coordinates) by full reference-centered SO(3) log and relative rotation log (6); drop three deterministic distances and the redundant absolute goal bypass, retaining the world hand anchor. Conditioning changes 37 to 25. Batch the four vector rotations. Fit only an initial orientation chart reference from D_N. A2/A3 feedback motivates not adding their mechanisms, but neither is a code/architecture parent. No edits to submitted A1-A3 and no performance-driven repeated debug.
